subject.title: [Feature]: feat: trigger session-memory hook on /compact command

question: Should bundled session-memory archive on compaction, and should that use `session:compact:before`, a literal `command:compact` trigger, or the existing memoryFlush/continuity path?
rationale: The source-proven gap remains, but OpenClaw now has separate compaction lifecycle hooks, default memoryFlush, and an open continuity-helper PR, so maintainers need to choose the permanent memory contract before implementation.

options.title: Use lifecycle compaction archive
options.body: Wire session-memory to a properly populated `session:compact:before` lifecycle event so manual and automatic compaction can both preserve pre-compaction context.

options.title: Keep memoryFlush as the answer
options.body: Document and refine `agents.defaults.compaction.memoryFlush` as the supported compaction-preservation path instead of changing bundled session-memory.

options.title: Wait for continuity helpers
options.body: Keep this issue open behind https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/84636 and decide compaction archival after the local continuity file format lands.

recommendation.title: Use lifecycle compaction archive
recommendation.body: Wire session-memory to a properly populated `session:compact:before` lifecycle event so manual and automatic compaction can both preserve pre-compaction context.

likelyOwner.reason: Current-line blame and commit metadata place steipete closest to the current session-memory, compaction hook, and memoryFlush implementation.
